The high heating capacity at 47°F (H47H Test) was to be equal to or higher than the capacity from the cooling bin A test. 3. The cut-out temperature was to be -15°F or lower and cut-in temperature was to be -10°F or lower as defined in AHRI 1340-2024 [2]. 4. The supply air temperature was to remain at 90°F or above down to 5°F outdoor air temperature with only the heat pump operating at maximum capacity. This requirement was to be evaluated at 5°F, 17°F, and 47°F outdoor air temperature integrated ventilation and heating efficiency metric for cold climates (IVHE ) tests and was to be evaluated only at the maximum capacity for each c temperature, which was to be Boost 2, Boost, or High operating level, whichever provides the highest capacity at each outdoor temperature. (These operating levels are defined in [2]). 5. The supplementary (backup) heating performance requirements were as follows. a. Manufacturers could offer electric resistance and/or natural gas backup heat. The combined capacity of the backup heat and heat pump were to be sized to cover the building load at -10°F outdoor air temperature. b. Control of backup heating was to be provided to allow continuously variable or staged heating levels. There was a requirement for peak demand, including defrost, that may drive heater staging design and control. Control of backup heat was to maximize use of the heat pump and to default to simultaneous operation for periods where the heat pump alone cannot meet the building load. Simultaneous heat pump and backup heat operation was to be checked at the -10°F CVP test point.
